name: Mary
interpretive_note: Christian traditions differ sharply on the identity of Jesus's "brothers" James, Joses, Judas, and Simon (Matthew 13:55; Mark 6:3). This entry follows the plain reading that they were Mary and Joseph's own children born after Jesus, which most Protestant interpreters hold; Catholic and Orthodox tradition instead reads them as Joseph's children from an earlier marriage or as Jesus's cousins, consistent with belief in Mary's perpetual virginity. Scripture does not settle the question explicitly.
source_summary: The mother of Jesus, a young unmarried woman of Nazareth who conceived by the Holy Spirit, bore and raised Jesus, and remained present through His ministry, death, and the early church's beginnings.
family_friendly_summary: Mary was a young woman from Nazareth engaged to a carpenter named Joseph when an angel named Gabriel appeared and told her she would give birth to God's own Son, Jesus, even though she was still a virgin. Mary was amazed and afraid, but she trusted God and said, "May it be done to me according to your word." She traveled to Bethlehem with Joseph, gave birth to Jesus in a stable, and later fled to Egypt to keep Him safe from a jealous king. Mary raised Jesus, watched Him begin His ministry, and stood near the cross when He died, grieving as any mother would. After Jesus rose from the dead, she prayed together with His followers, waiting for the Holy Spirit.
adult_story: Mary was a young, unmarried woman of Nazareth, betrothed to Joseph, when the angel Gabriel announced she would conceive by the Holy Spirit and bear the Son of God, though she had never been with a man (Luke 1:26-38). Facing the risk of scandal under the law for apparent unfaithfulness, she answered simply, "Behold, the bondslave of the Lord; may it be done to me according to your word," and praised God in the song known as the Magnificat (Luke 1:46-55). She traveled to Bethlehem while pregnant, gave birth to Jesus among animals because there was no room at the inn, and treasured these events in her heart (Luke 2:5-19). She and Joseph fled to Egypt to escape Herod's massacre of infant boys (Matthew 2). At Cana, she prompted Jesus's first miracle, telling the servants, "Whatever He says to you, do it" (John 2:1-5). She bore other sons and daughters with Joseph after Jesus's birth (Matthew 13:55; Mark 6:3). Years later, she stood at the foot of the cross as Jesus died, and He entrusted her care to His disciple John (John 19:26-27). After the resurrection, she joined the apostles in prayer awaiting the Holy Spirit (Acts 1:14) -- her story is one of costly, uncertain obedience to a promise she could not fully understand.
devotionals: Mary said, 'may it be done to me according to your word.' May we trust God that same way, even when we don't understand his plan.
At Cana, Mary told the servants, 'whatever he says to you, do it.' That's still the best advice anyone could give us about following Jesus.
Mary stood at the cross and watched Jesus die. His love held nothing back for us, even to that moment.
